stem: The lattice enthalpy of an ionic solid is the energy

stem: For Na(g) -> Na+(g) the ionisation enthalpy is 495.8 kJ mol-1, and for Cl(g) -> Cl-(g) the electron gain enthalpy is -348.7 kJ mol-1. Though the sum of these is positive, solid NaCl forms readily. What makes its formation favourable?

The large energy released when the gaseous ions pack together into the crystal lattice
The sharing of electron pairs between Na and Cl atoms inside the crystal lattice
The energy absorbed in converting solid sodium metal into gaseous sodium atoms

Option A states the opposite of the data, NaCl is ionic not covalent, and an energy-absorbing step cannot make formation favourable.

stem: NH3 and NF3 are both pyramidal with one lone pair on N, and fluorine is more electronegative than nitrogen. Yet NF3 has a much smaller dipole moment than NH3. Which is the best explanation?
options: In NH3 the lone-pair moment adds to the bond moments, but in NF3 it opposes them
In NF3 the N-F bonds are nearly non-polar because N and F lie in the same period
In NF3 the lone pair is used in bonding, so only the N-F bond moments remain
NF3 is planar, so its three N-F bond moments cancel out almost completely
explanation: Correct option: (A). In NH3 the N-H bond dipoles point towards N, the same direction as the lone-pair moment, so they add. In NF3 the N-F bond dipoles point towards F, away from the lone pair, so the orbital moment of the lone pair partly cancels the resultant bond moment. N-F bonds are clearly polar, the lone pair in NF3 is not used in bonding, and NF3 is pyramidal, not planar.

stem: In SF4, sulphur has four bond pairs and one lone pair in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement, and the lone pair takes an equatorial position. Why is this position preferred?
options: An equatorial lone pair has two repulsions at 90 degrees, an axial one would have three
An equatorial lone pair is closer to the nucleus, so it has lower energy than an axial one
An axial lone pair would make the molecule planar, which VSEPR theory does not allow
Axial positions are reserved for bond pairs because axial bonds are always stronger
explanation: Correct option: (A). Repulsions at 90 degrees are the strongest. stem: As two hydrogen atoms approach each other to form H2, how does the potential energy of the system change?
options: It increases steadily until the bond forms
It stays constant until the orbitals overlap
It decreases to a minimum at the bond length
It decreases steadily at all distances
explanation: Correct option: (C). stem: Which statement about a bonding molecular orbital is correct?

HF molecules are linear and so cannot form any hydrogen bonds in the liquid state
explanation: Correct option: (A). Each water molecule has two H atoms and two lone pairs on O, so it can take part in up to four hydrogen bonds and builds an extensive three-dimensional network. An HF molecule has only one H atom, so it forms on average about two hydrogen bonds (zig-zag chains). The total hydrogen bonding per molecule is therefore greater in water. Water's hydrogen bonds are intermolecular, fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen, and HF does form hydrogen bonds.
